🚨 FORECLOSURE WATCH // Bank repossessions jumped 42% in August 🏠

Lenders repossessed 5,794 homes in August, up 42% from a year earlier and up 22% from July, according to ATTOM. Texas accounted for nearly a third of them.

 * 🏠 Completed repossessions: 5,794, up 42% YoY, up 22% MoM
 * 🤠 Texas: 1,835, the most of any state (California next at 589)
 * 🏙️ Houston 448, Dallas 402, San Antonio 256 led all metros
 * 📋 Total filings: 40,277, up 13% YoY
 * 📉 New starts: 25,894, up just 7% YoY

▬▬▬

⚠️ THE CATCH
Completed foreclosures are a lagging indicator, marking the end of a process that started months or years ago, while new starts grew only 7%. ATTOM notes total activity remains below pre-pandemic norms, so this is a surge from a low base, not a 2008 replay. The data is August's, released weeks ago and repackaged in today's headlines.

▬▬▬

🧠 THE TAKEAWAY
The distress is real but concentrated: three Texas metros drove nearly a fifth of all repossessions. The number to watch is new starts, and those are barely growing. Are banks working through old backlog, or is fresh distress building? 👇 NFA
